items.name: Rectangle primitive (stroke + fill + opacity)
items.spec:
Add `clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/primitives/rectangle.{h,cpp}` — screen-agnostic Clay helper for a flat-colored rectangle with optional stroke and optional fill opacity. API shape (final names yours; spirit of the constraints binding):

- Take ALL color/width values as REQUIRED parameters (compile-time, not opts-struct defaults) — match the precedent set by commit 63c779d. No lobby-coupled defaults.
- Knobs: fillPaletteColor (Uint8 or 'no fill' sentinel), fillOpacity (0.0–1.0 or palette-alpha-index), strokePaletteColor (Uint8 or 'no stroke'), strokeWidth (Uint8, fixed 1 px is fine for now if you want to simplify), plus sizing (caller-provided width/height OR sized-by-parent if used inside a flex container).
- The primitive emits ONE Clay element with `.backgroundColor` and `.border` configured from the params. No CUSTOM render command unless opacity-blending requires it (see C1).
- Add a render test at `clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/rectangle_test.cpp` that renders 4 variants: stroke-only, fill-only, fill+stroke, fill-with-opacity-over-an-existing-color. Wired through the JSON-lines control op pattern used by other primitive tests.
- Test references at `tests/lobby-clay/rectangle_test/` (reference.png + run.sh).

NOTE: this primitive will be renamed Rectangle→Box in the next item (C0b). The historical name 'Rectangle' is preserved here as the record of what shipped first.

items.name: Rename Rectangle primitive → Box (canonical UI vocabulary)
items.spec:
Pure rename. 'Rectangle' implies a geometric shape; the canonical web/UI vocabulary for a generic styled container is 'Box' (Chakra, Mantine, NativeBase, Tamagui, Material Box). Clay itself doesn't name this concept — every CLAY({...}) is just 'an element' — so the choice is downstream. Box is shorter, role-neutral, and pairs naturally with future Row/Column/Stack siblings.

Mechanics (use `git mv` everywhere to preserve history):

1. `git mv clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/primitives/rectangle.h clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/primitives/box.h`
2. `git mv clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/primitives/rectangle.cpp clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/primitives/box.cpp`
3. `git mv clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/rectangle_test.cpp clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/box_test.cpp`
4. `git mv tests/lobby-clay/rectangle_test tests/lobby-clay/box_test`

Inside the moved files:

5. Header guard: `SILENCER_UI_CLAY_PRIMITIVES_RECTANGLE_H` → `SILENCER_UI_CLAY_PRIMITIVES_BOX_H` in box.h.
6. Function rename: `silencer::ui::primitives::Rectangle(...)` → `Box(...)` everywhere (header, impl, test, any caller — there shouldn't be any non-test callers yet because C3+ haven't run).
7. `#include "rectangle.h"` → `#include "box.h"` in box.cpp and box_test.cpp.
8. Docstring rewrites in box.h: every mention of 'rectangle' → 'box'. The word 'rectangle' can stay where it refers to the GEOMETRIC primitive being drawn (e.g., 'emits a rectangle on screen') vs. the primitive's NAME.
9. In `clients/silencer/src/net/controldispatch.cpp`: rename the control op `clay_rectangle_test` → `clay_box_test`.
10. In `clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/clay_bridge.h`: rename the forward decl `RunRectangleTest` → `RunBoxTest`.
11. In `tests/lobby-clay/box_test/run.sh`: update the `cli` invocation from `clay_rectangle_test` to `clay_box_test`.
12. Refresh CMake source list because renamed files don't auto-pick-up: `cmake -B build -S clients/silencer`.
13. Build + run the test. Pixdiff MUST still be 0.0000% — this is a pure rename, no visual change. If pixdiff changes, a string slipped through; find it.

Nothing else changes — same API shape, same params, same rendered pixels. The `passes` flag for C0 stays true; this iteration's commit just renames artifacts.

items.name: Box stroke halos (multi-tone outer + inner rings)
items.spec:
The bright stroke in the lobby BG sprite is technically a 1-px palette idx 216 line — Clay's default border reproduces those pixels exactly — BUT the visual depth around it comes from the BG sprite's decorative dithered framing (palette idx 75 / 81 / 211 in 1–2 px bands on either side). Once C7 drops the BG sprite, those framing pixels vanish and the bare 1-px stroke looks naked against flat black. To recreate the legacy chrome depth without baking back any texture, extend the Box primitive with multi-tone halos: bands of color around the primary stroke that the bridge renders procedurally.

API additions to `clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/primitives/box.{h,cpp}` (post-C0b rename):

- `strokeOuterHaloColor: Uint8` (0 = no outer halo)
- `strokeOuterHaloWidth: Uint8` (px count, 0–2)
- `strokeInnerHaloColor: Uint8` (0 = no inner halo)
- `strokeInnerHaloWidth: Uint8` (px count, 0–2)

All four are REQUIRED parameters — match 63c779d precedent. The four-zero case (no halos) MUST fall through to the existing Clay `.border` path (cheap; no new render commands).

When ANY halo is non-zero, the bridge routes through a new `CustomKind::BoxStroke` (or similar — name yours) that renders the stroke as concentric inset rectangles: outermost first (at the box's outer edge), then progressively inward, ending with the primary stroke. Inner halos extend further inward from the primary. Each ring is 1 px wide repeated `<thing>HaloWidth` times.

Use the inspection helper at `/tmp/inspect_lobby_stroke.py` (already on disk) to sample the actual chrome halo colors at multiple corners of the lobby BG. The bright primary is consistently idx 216; the outer halo around it is approximately idx 75 (rgb 8,40,8) one ring out, and idx 211 (rgb 0,32,0) at two rings out. The inner halo is approximately idx 81. Sample at 3–4 different lobby rectangle edges to confirm consistency before committing the canonical values.

Document the canonical values in `docs/plans/lobby-chrome-rectangles.md` (the doc C2 will create) so each panel item (C3–C7) passes the same halo params. Suggested default for the lobby's chrome rectangles: `strokeColor=216, strokeOuterHaloColor=75, strokeOuterHaloWidth=1, strokeInnerHaloColor=81, strokeInnerHaloWidth=1`. The agent on C2 fine-tunes after sampling.

Update the box_test scene to add a 5th variant: box with halos on (visible against the test scene's existing backgrounds). Add a sixth panel-style test scene: a Box rendered with the lobby's canonical halo params against a flat black background — this is the visual the user will review when C0c lands.
items.pass_check: Build green. `tests/lobby-clay/box_test/run.sh` PASS — existing four variants unchanged + a fifth halo-variant region in the layout. `tests/lobby-clay/box_halo_test/run.sh` PASS — single Box with the canonical lobby halo params, rendered against flat black, pixdiff < 1% vs reference.png. Screenshot DM'd. No lobby includes in box.{h,cpp}.

items.name: Box vs legacy chat-box parity validation (side-by-side DM)
items.spec:
Before any panel item consumes Box's halo API at scale, validate that a Box with sampled halo colors visually matches a known legacy lobby chrome rectangle — concretely, the **chat-box outer frame** (the most prominent rectangle in the lobby). Deliverable: a side-by-side PNG DM'd to the user showing the legacy chrome's chat-box region alongside a Clay-only Box rendered at the same dimensions with sampled halo params. The user reviews and signs off (or asks for halo-API revisions) before C2 commits the canonical values.

Mechanics:

1. **Sample the legacy chat-box stroke + halo.** The chat-box in the legacy lobby chrome lives roughly at x=15, y=216, w=368, h=234 (from the deleted `clients/silencer/src/ui/screens/lobby/panels/chat_panel.cpp` — see git history). Use `/tmp/inspect_lobby_stroke.py` (already on disk) as a starting point; extend it if needed to sample around (15, 216) and at all four corners of the chat-box stroke. Record (primary palette idx, outer halo idx at 1px out, outer halo idx at 2px out, inner halo idx at 1px in, inner halo idx at 2px in). Determine widths (1 or 2 px each side) from the consistency of the dithered pattern.

2. **Crop the legacy chat-box from the BG sprite.** Using the `/tmp/dump_lobby_bg.py` decoder, write a small companion script `/tmp/crop_lobby_chat_box.py` that reads the decoded PNG and writes `/tmp/legacy_chat_box.png` — a 380×246 crop covering the chat-box rectangle plus a 6 px padding margin so the chrome strokes are clearly visible against the surrounding context.

3. **Render the Clay Box at the same dimensions.** Add a new control op `clay_box_parity_chat` (mirror the `clay_box_test` pattern). The scene renders ONE `Box` at chat-box width/height (368×234) with the sampled halo params from step 1, positioned at (6, 6) inside a 380×246 viewport with flat-black background. Dump as `/tmp/clay_chat_box.png`.

4. **Compose side-by-side.** Write `/tmp/compose_parity_dm.py` that takes the two PNGs and produces `/tmp/box_chat_parity.png` — both images side-by-side at native resolution (~760×246), with a 1-px white separator and small text labels 'LEGACY' / 'CLAY BOX' at the top of each.

5. **DM the side-by-side** to the user with a brief caption listing the canonical halo params used (e.g. 'stroke=216, outer={75, 211}, inner={81}, w_outer=2, w_inner=1'). The DM is the central deliverable of this iteration — make sure it goes out cleanly with the attachment.

6. **Self-grade.** Document the comparison in `progress.txt`: which halo colors landed correctly, which look off, whether the user is likely to request API changes (e.g., 'inner halo needs a second ring' or 'outer halo needs 3 distinct shades not 2'). Be honest — false reassurance wastes the user's time.

7. **Provisionally pass.** Set `passes=true` and commit. If the user reviews the DM and isn't satisfied, they'll insert a follow-up item (C0e or a halo-API revision) — that's a feature of the loop, not a bug of this iteration. Better to flip and let the user redirect than to stall on visual judgment.

C2 (which canonicalizes the halo values for the entire lobby) consumes the result of this iteration. The agent on C0d MUST write the chosen halo params into a small `docs/plans/lobby-chrome-rectangles.md` stub (just the chat-box row for now) so C2's full coordinate table extends rather than rediscovers them.

items.name: Bridge: alpha-blended Box fills via palette alphaed LUT
items.spec:
The current Clay bridge dispatches RECTANGLE by writing a single palette index per pixel — no alpha. For the Box primitive's `fillOpacity`, the bridge must route to the renderer's existing palette-blend path. Read `clients/silencer/src/render/palette.cpp` (look for `alphaed`) to understand the LUT: `alphaed[palette][src*256 + dst]` returns the blended palette index. Each Box pixel at opacity α maps to `alphaed[…][srcColor*256 + dstColor]` with α as the LUT bank selector (or, simpler first cut: pick one alpha level for now, e.g. 50%, and document that opacity is currently quantized to that single level — full N-level alpha can come later if needed).

Extend the bridge in `clients/silencer/src/ui/clay/clay_bridge.cpp`. If the simplest path is a new CustomKind (e.g. `CustomKind::FillBlend`) that the Box primitive routes through when `fillOpacity < 1.0`, that's fine — but prefer just enhancing the existing RECTANGLE dispatch to read the userData for an optional opacity hint.

Add a smoke test: a fully-opaque red box underneath a 50%-opaque blue box should produce a known mid-tone palette index in the overlap region. Pixdiff against a hand-crafted reference < 0.5%.

items.name: Complete partial migrations in C3/C4/C5 (real flex, no wrap-shortcut, padding, alignment)
items.spec:
User reviewed the C3/C4/C5 screenshots and flagged clear text misalignment. Root cause: those iterations did PARTIAL migrations — some elements moved inside their Box, others still `floating @ROOT (x, y)` at their original legacy coords. Result: misaligned text crashes against the new Box strokes, baked BG strokes don't overlap the new Clay strokes, no breathing room from chrome.

Audit every panel migrated so far and complete the migration.

## Audit

1. `clients/silencer/src/ui/screens/lobby_clay/lobby_clay_screen.cpp` — title bar elements (LobbyTitle, LobbyVer, LobbyMapName, LobbyGoBackWrap). Currently 8 `floating` mentions; goal: 0 or 1 (one ROOT-attached chrome wrapper at most).
2. `clients/silencer/src/ui/screens/lobby_clay/clay_character_panel.cpp` — username, agency toggles, stats rows. Currently 2 `floating` mentions; goal: 0.
3. `clients/silencer/src/ui/screens/lobby_clay/clay_chat_panel.cpp` — channel header, chat textbox, presence textbox, chat input. Currently 3 `floating` mentions; goal: 0.

For each `floating @ROOT (x, y)` element found:

- Move it inside its containing Box via flex layout (`.layout = { ... }`).
- Use the Box's `.padding` for breathing room from the stroke (default 4 px each edge unless content is supposed to bleed to an edge for a specific reason).
- Use `.childGap` for spacing between siblings.
- Use `.childAlignment` for centering / justifying.
- DELETE the `.floating = { .attachTo = CLAY_ATTACH_TO_ROOT, .offset = { x, y } }` config.

Exception: a parent Box may itself be `floating @ROOT` to position the whole panel at a known screen coord — that's OK and counts as the allowed `1 or fewer` floating reference per file.

## Padding

Each migrated Box adds `.padding = { left, right, top, bottom }` in its `.layout`. Default 4 each edge. Tune visually if a specific element looks too close or too far from the stroke.

## Baked-vs-Clay stroke overlap

During this transition phase (before C7 drops LobbyBg), the baked BG strokes and the Clay-drawn Box strokes MUST align to within 1 px so they read as ONE visible stroke. If you see double-stroking in your screenshot, the Box's `.floating.offset` or its outer width/height is wrong. Fix it.

## Anti-shortcut

Do NOT use the wrap-shortcut: `CLAY({...wrapper...}) { existing_floating_subtree(); }`. The wrap makes the inspector see children as nested but the children still position absolutely. Each `floating @ROOT` element MUST be deleted and reborn as a flex child. See RALPH.md's 'Anti-pattern: wrap-shortcut migration' section.

## Programmatic verification (REQUIRED)

Write `/tmp/verify_panel_alignment.py` that loads `/tmp/ralph-shots/iter-C5b.png`, samples specific (x, y) positions, and asserts pixel palette indices. Sample positions to validate:

- Title bar stroke at its left edge (idx 216 expected).
- Title bar interior at (left_stroke_x + 6, mid_y) — expect a text-color palette index where 'S' of 'Silencer' should be (around idx 152 for the title-effect color), NOT the stroke idx, confirming text has padding.
- Character Box at its top-left corner stroke (idx 216 expected).
- Character Box interior at (top_left + 6, top_left + 6) — expect NON-stroke index.
- Chat Box stroke alignment with baked BG stroke (sample (chat_baked_x, chat_baked_y) — should still be idx 216 because Clay's stroke overlaps the baked stroke).
- Print PASS/FAIL per sample. The script's overall exit code is 0 only if all samples pass.

Include the script's full output in your progress.txt entry for this iteration.

## Visual self-verification (REQUIRED, in addition to programmatic)

Use the Read tool on `/tmp/ralph-shots/iter-C5b.png` to actually look at the image. Confirm:

- No text crashes against any stroke.
- No visible double-stroking between baked + Clay rectangles.
- The lobby is reasonably coherent vs. C2's documented coords.

If the screenshot still looks wrong after the work, leave `passes=false` and document the specific visual issue + which Box has the problem.

## Discord DM

Send the screenshot + the programmatic verification script's output (paste the PASS/FAIL summary in the caption).
